question: According to the Transformer paper, what property of recurrent models prevents parallelization within training examples, and why does it matter more for long sequences?
final_text: I couldn't find this in the passages I retrieved from the three papers, so I won't guess. I searched: AIAYN §1 Introduction; AIAYN §abstract Abstract; AIAYN §6.3 English Constituency Parsing; HNET §1 Introduction.
drafts: Recurrent models factor computation along the symbol positions of the input and output sequences, generating each hidden state as a function of the previous hidden state, which inherently sequentially precludes parallelization within training examples, and this becomes critical at longer sequence lengths because memory constraints limit batching across examples [AIAYN:1:c002].

Recurrent models typically factor computation along the symbol positions of the input and output sequences, aligning the positions to steps in computation time, they generate a sequence of hidden states h_t, as a function of the previous hidden state h_t-1 and the input for position t [AIAYN:1:c002]. This inherently sequential nature precludes parallelization within training examples, which becomes critical at longer sequence lengths, as memory constraints limit batching across examples [AIAYN:1:c002].
